title: Melanoma (melanocytes) shares neural crest origin with dorsal root ganglia
vignette: A 45-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department after a generalized tonic-clonic seizure. She reports no prior history of seizures, but she has noticed right arm weakness over the last week. Her family history is significant for skin cancer in her mother. Physical examination shows a skin lesion measuring 13 mm on her back, which is asymmetric with irregular borders and variable pigmentation. The cells responsible for this patient's lesion most likely share a common embryologic origin with which of the following?

clues.text: right arm weakness over the last week
clues.note: New focal neurologic deficits and a seizure raise concern for brain metastases - the CNS is a common site of melanoma spread.

clues.text: asymmetric with irregular borders and variable pigmentation
clues.note: Asymmetry, Border irregularity, Color variation, and Diameter >=6 mm (ABCDE) are features of MELANOMA - a malignancy of melanocytes.

whatMatters: The pigmented, ABCDE-positive lesion is a MELANOMA, arising from MELANOCYTES, which are derived from NEURAL CREST cells. Among the options, DORSAL ROOT GANGLIA are also neural crest derivatives. Answer C.
strategy: Identify melanoma -> melanocytes -> NEURAL CREST origin, then pick the other neural crest derivative. Neural crest gives rise to melanocytes, dorsal root/autonomic ganglia, Schwann cells, adrenal MEDULLA, enteric ganglia, pia/arachnoid, and branchial-arch cartilage/bones. Reject non-neural-crest structures: adrenal CORTEX (mesoderm), anterior pituitary (surface ectoderm/Rathke pouch), pancreas (endoderm), and sweat glands (surface ectoderm).

eliminations.label: Adrenal cortex - mesoderm
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: the steroid-producing outer adrenal gland. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: the adrenal CORTEX is MESODERM-derived; only the adrenal MEDULLA (chromaffin cells) is neural crest. ✅ Correct if: asking about mesodermal derivatives (or the adrenal medulla for neural crest).

eliminations.label: Anterior pituitary - surface ectoderm (Rathke pouch)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: the adenohypophysis. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it arises from SURFACE ECTODERM (Rathke pouch), not neural crest. ✅ Correct if: surface ectoderm derivatives (lens, epidermis, adenohypophysis).

eliminations.label: Pancreas - endoderm
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: an endodermal foregut derivative. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it comes from ENDODERM (gut tube), not neural crest. ✅ Correct if: endodermal (GI/glandular) derivatives.

eliminations.label: Sweat glands - surface ectoderm
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: epidermal appendage glands. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: sweat glands (and epidermis) derive from SURFACE ECTODERM, not neural crest. ✅ Correct if: epidermis/adnexal (surface ectoderm) structures.

reasoning: The pigmented ABCDE lesion is a melanoma
Dorsal root ganglia are also neural crest derivatives -> answer C
mechanism: MELANOMA is a malignancy of MELANOCYTES, the pigment-producing cells of the epidermis (recognized clinically by the ABCDE criteria: Asymmetry, Border irregularity, Color variation, Diameter >=6 mm, Evolving). Melanocytes are derived from NEURAL CREST CELLS - multipotent, migratory cells that originate at the border of the neural plate/ectoderm and give rise to a diverse lineage: melanocytes, sensory (DORSAL ROOT) ganglia, sympathetic and parasympathetic (autonomic) and enteric ganglia, Schwann cells, the ADRENAL MEDULLA (chromaffin cells), pia and arachnoid mater, aorticopulmonary septum/endocardial cushions, odontoblasts, and branchial-arch bones/cartilage of the face and skull. Because dorsal root ganglia are neural crest derivatives, they share a common embryologic origin with melanocytes/melanoma. Melanoma is aggressive and commonly metastasizes to the brain (explaining this patient's seizure and focal weakness). The distractors derive from other germ layers: adrenal cortex (mesoderm), anterior pituitary and sweat glands (surface ectoderm), and pancreas (endoderm).

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Embryo > neural crest derivatives: melanocytes, dorsal root/autonomic/enteric ganglia, Schwann cells, adrenal medulla, pia/arachnoid, aorticopulmonary septum, branchial-arch skeleton, odontoblasts; melanoma = melanocyte malignancy (neural crest).

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Melanoma = melanocytes = neural crest; dorsal root ganglia are also neural crest.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on neural crest, melanocytes/melanoma, dorsal root ganglia, adrenal cortex vs medulla, or germ layers? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Adrenal cortex = mesoderm; anterior pituitary/sweat glands = surface ectoderm; pancreas = endoderm.

difficulty.label: 🖼️ Imaging / diagram
difficulty.text: Skin lesion (stem image): asymmetric, irregular-bordered, variably pigmented lesion = melanoma (melanocytes, neural crest); shares origin with dorsal root ganglia.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: melanocytes (melanoma) = neural crest; also DRG, adrenal medulla, Schwann cells, enteric ganglia.

keywords.front: Melanoma cell of origin / germ layer

keywords.back: Melanocytes, DRG/autonomic ganglia, Schwann, adrenal medulla, pia/arachnoid, branchial arch skeleton
Asymmetry, Border, Color, Diameter >=6 mm, Evolving
Brain (also lung, liver) - can cause seizures

firstAid.detail: Embryo: melanocytes = neural crest; shares origin with dorsal root ganglia.

memoryHook: Melanoma = melanocytes = neural crest, the same 'crest crew' that builds the dorsal root ganglia (and the adrenal medulla, Schwann cells...).
